short.q: Explain the difference between extreme and boundary test data for a range of 1 to 20.
short.model: Extreme data is valid data at the limits of the range, such as 1 and 20. Boundary data is the limit and the nearest value outside it, such as 20 and 21 or 1 and 0, to show where the program switches from accepting to rejecting.
points: Boundary: limit plus nearest rejected value (e.g. 20 and 21)

short.q: Show the list 8 3 6 1 after the first pass of a bubble sort into ascending order.
short.model: 3 6 1 8. 8 and 3 swap, 8 and 6 swap, 8 and 1 swap, so the largest value 8 moves to the end.

short.q: A user enters their age as 'twelve'. Name the validation check that would reject it and explain why.
short.model: A type check would reject it because the age must be a number (integer) and 'twelve' is text.
points: Value is text, not an integer

short.q: Explain why validation cannot guarantee that data is correct.
short.model: Validation only checks that the data is reasonable and follows the rules. Data can pass the checks but still be wrong, e.g. an age of 17 typed instead of 71 is inside the valid range.
points: Only checks data is reasonable/meets rules

short.q: Write pseudocode to count how many of the 20 values in the array Scores[1:20] are greater than 50.
short.model:
Count ← 0
FOR I ← 1 TO 20
  IF Scores[I] > 50 THEN
    Count ← Count + 1
  ENDIF
NEXT I
OUTPUT Count
